content.6.1.2.2_Pre-treatment_in_patients_with_n: Randomized trials (ACCOAST) showed no ischaemic benefit and higher bleeding risk with prasugrel pre-treatment in NSTE-ACS. ISAR-REACT 5 data suggested a ticagrelor-based routine pre-treatment strategy was inferior to a prasugrel-based strategy with deferred loading dose in NSTE-ACS. The DUBIUS trial comparing upstream vs downstream oral P2Y12 administration was stopped early for futility with no difference between strategies in patients scheduled for coronary angiography within 72 h.
content.6.1.2.3_Summary_of_pre-treatment_strateg: For STEMI patients undergoing PPCI, pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered. For NSTE-ACS, routine pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor before coronary anatomy is known is not recommended when an early invasive strategy (<24 h) is planned. For anticipated delays to angiography (>24 h) in NSTE-ACS, pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered based on bleeding risk. If ACS patients proceed to PCI without prior P2Y12 receptor inhibitor pre-treatment, a loading dose at the time of PCI is recommended.
content.6.1.3_Intravenous_antiplatelet_drugs: Peri-interventional intravenous antiplatelet drugs include P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (cangrelor) and glycoprotein (GP) IIb/IIIa inhibitors (eptifibatide, tirofiban). Most GP IIb/IIIa trials pre-date routine DAPT; there is no strong evidence of additional benefit for routine GP IIb/IIIa use in ACS patients scheduled for coronary angiography. GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors may be considered as bailout therapy for no-reflow or thrombotic complications during PCI. Early initiation of DAPT including a loading dose of a potent P2Y12 receptor inhibitor has been used in trials.

trials_and_evidence.name: ACCOAST
trials_and_evidence.finding: No ischaemic benefit and higher bleeding risk with prasugrel pre-treatment in NSTE-ACS.

trials_and_evidence.name: ISAR-REACT 5
trials_and_evidence.finding: Ticagrelor-based routine pre-treatment inferior to prasugrel-based strategy with deferred loading dose in NSTE-ACS.

trials_and_evidence.name: DUBIUS
trials_and_evidence.finding: Stopped early for futility; no difference between upstream vs downstream oral P2Y12 administration for patients scheduled for coronary angiography within 72 h.

clinical_recommendations: Consider P2Y12 receptor inhibitor pre-treatment in STEMI undergoing PPCI.
Do not routinely pre-treat NSTE-ACS patients with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor if early invasive strategy (<24 h) is planned.
Consider pre-treatment in NSTE-ACS if angiography is anticipated to be delayed (>24 h) after assessing bleeding risk.
If no P2Y12 pre-treatment before PCI, give a loading dose at time of PCI.
Use IV GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors selectively as bailout for no-reflow or thrombotic complications; routine use not supported by strong evidence.

genes.context: The guideline repeatedly refers to the P2Y12 receptor and P2Y12 receptor inhibitors (oral and intravenous, e.g., cangrelor) in recommendations about pre-treatment strategies for STEMI, NSTE-ACS and peri-procedural management in patients undergoing PCI; discusses timing, bleeding risk, and trial data (DUBIUS, ISAR-REACT 5, ACCOAST).
